topic: the debug-with-cli skill: driving shell commands on remote machines from a Sauna agent via Tailscale Funnel + Bearer-auth HTTP bridge

subtopics.scope: Why the bridge is HTTP-only via the Sauna auth proxy: the sandbox has network access but no tailscale binary and cannot ssh to non-public hosts; the target box runs a Bearer-auth HTTP server returning {stdout, stderr, returncode}; argv shape as a feature (no injection, no quoting).

When to apply the skill (Sauna cannot otherwise reach the machine; read logs/inspect state/probe loop; 20-min CI round-trips to 20-second curls) and the four do-NOT-use boundaries (HTTP API exists, one-off log read, no Tailscale, needs real PTY).

The one-time target-box setup: Tailscale install via install.sh, headless auth with a non-ephemeral reusable auth key, tailscale funnel --bg 8080, funnel status, the https://<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net URL shape.
seed_queries: tailscale funnel setup background port ts.net URL
tailscale ephemeral vs non-ephemeral nodes auth key reusable

subtopics.scope: The Sauna-side setup: connect_account with connection_type keys (not mcp), auth_type bearer, auth_strategy static inject bearer, token field, and proxy auto-injection of the Authorization header; verify 401 without auth then 200 with auth.
seed_queries: RFC 6750 bearer token Authorization header HTTP scheme
bearer token authentication HTTP proxy auto-injection

subtopics.scope: The ~50-LOC Python stdlib bridge internals: BaseHTTPRequestHandler + HTTPServer on 127.0.0.1:8080, hmac.compare_digest Bearer check, JSON body {command, timeout, cwd}, subprocess.run(capture_output=True, text=True), TimeoutExpired to 408, quiet log_message.

POST /run request shape: command is a JSON array of argv strings passed to subprocess.run with shell=False; no pipes at the bridge (bash -c via argv is the escape hatch), sudo -n is mandatory, per-call env not supported, cwd field.
seed_queries: python subprocess.run argv list shell False command injection
subprocess.run timeout capture_output text parameters docs

subtopics.scope: The argv-audit-to-tty pattern for user observability: banner via printf %b to /dev/ttyS2 then run with tee -a, repr() quoting of argv elements for the inner bash -c, tee -a not >, and the two-POST rule for multi-line content (write to host /tmp first, then cat to TTY).

The security model: 256-bit openssl rand -hex 32 token, TLS terminated at the Funnel edge, bind 127.0.0.1 never 0.0.0.0, token stored in /etc mode 600 env file, argv-only subprocess, constant-time hmac.compare_digest, journald audit posture.
seed_queries: hmac.compare_digest constant time string comparison python
openssl rand hex 32 token entropy 256 bits

subtopics.scope: The six rejected alternatives and why: sparfenyuk mcp-proxy (no inbound auth), punkpeye mcp-proxy (Node dep + X-API-Key), Cloudflare Tunnel + Access (per-call OIDC), mTLS (no cert store in sandbox), adding the sandbox to the tailnet (extra infra, no auth change), Funnel ACL grants (sandbox is not a tailnet user).
seed_queries: sparfenyuk mcp-proxy stdio HTTP bridge GitHub
cloudflare tunnel access oidc self-hosted app

subtopics.scope: The anti-pattern list (0.0.0.0 bind, plaintext token logging, short tokens, string commands, Funnel to exposed ports, sudo without -n, skipping the local smoke test, mistaking Cloudflare 530/1016 for auth) plus loading constraints (argv-only, no request logging by default, one bridge per machine, token rotation cadence).
